$comment: Canonical cases for projecting SCORM 2004's two status axes onto the single
SCORM 1.2 lesson_status the platform stores, reports, bills and relays.
The rule has to run in three places: SQL, for the hosted player's rollup over
progress.cmi_result; C#, for the dispatch save which projects from the incoming
payload; and TypeScript, for the shim relaying a result to a host LMS. A rule
written three times will disagree with itself eventually, so all three read
this file and are asserted against it rather than against each other.
THE RULE. Completion says whether the learner finished. Success says how.
- A failure is terminal and overrides everything. Never report a learner as
complete when the course said they failed.
- A pass does NOT override an explicit incomplete. A learner who passed the
quiz but has not finished the course has not finished the course, and this
platform's completions drive certificates and billing.
- Otherwise completion decides, and an unknown completion reads as
incomplete rather than not attempted, because 2004 courses commonly leave
completion_status unknown for the whole of an attempt that is plainly
underway.
1.2 has 'browsed' and 2004 has no equivalent (cmi.mode = browse is a different
statement), so no 2004 input ever projects to it.
THE ROLLUP RULE. A course is made of launchable activities. Nothing
implements this yet: the cases are written first, deliberately, so the SQL and
C# copies have something to disagree with before either one exists.
- A single-activity course projects its one activity unchanged. 519 of 528
live courses are that shape, so the guarantee is structural rather than
checked case by case. The lone exception is a single asset, which records
nothing today and completes on delivery under this rule.
- An asset is terminal once delivered. It has no API to report through, so
being served to the learner is the only signal that exists.
- A SCO is terminal at passed, failed or completed. Incomplete, browsed, not
attempted and silence are not.
- While any activity is not terminal the course is incomplete, so one failed
SCO does not end a course the learner could still finish. Once every
activity is terminal a failure decides, then a pass, then completed.
- Nothing reported anywhere stays nothing reported. Every activity explicitly
not attempted reads as not attempted.
Activity counts below are representative and the rule does not depend on them.
Browsed being non-terminal in a rollup is the one call here not forced by
THE RULE above, and is the first thing to revisit if a 1.2 package argues
with it.

status.why: a failure is terminal even when the course is finished
passed the quiz, has not finished the course
a failure is terminal even mid-course
contradictory, but an explicit pass is the more specific claim
attempt underway and the course has said nothing
1.2 browsed has no 2004 source but must survive
empty is the same as absent
a stale 1.2 default must not mask a live 2004 status

a single-SCO failure follows THE RULE unchanged
browsed survives only because a single activity projects unchanged
one SCO that reported nothing stays nothing
a lone asset completes on delivery, which is a deliberate change: today it records nothing
a lone asset never reached has still reported nothing
every activity terminal and graded
the multi-SCO bug in full: today this reports passed on the strength of SCO 1 alone
a second SCO underway holds the course open
a failure does not end a course the learner could still finish
every activity terminal, so the failure decides
finished, nothing graded
any grade makes the course graded
explicitly not started

a hundredths tail is dropped, not kept
